framework_metadata.description: Plain CUDA allocator segments, so the copy-engine IPC all-to-all can start.
framework_metadata.notes: Derived from `b200-2gpu` (the profile B300 selects). Audit 2026-10-23 (Cosmos3/Wan2.2 finding 1): the harness exports PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True (scripts/devbox_run_cases.sh); sharing an expandable segment needs pidfd_getfd, which RunPod containers deny, so every sglang SP cell of the round logged 'IPC all-to-all (multi-rank) unavailable (pidfd_getfd: Operation not permitted); using NCCL'. TRT-LLM already carries this override for the same reason. Accept the arm only if that line is absent. Promoted from cand-noexp by the 2026-10-22 4xB300 fourth-wave A/B: 63.78 s against b200-2gpu 66.05 s at 49 forwards (FA4 67.42). RunPod containers deny pidfd_getfd, so under the harness's expandable_segments:True sglang's multi-rank IPC all-to-all fell back to NCCL ('IPC all-to-all (multi-rank) unavailable'); sglang#45948 (merged 2026-10-23, not in this round's pin 82f7249c) fixes it in sglang. TRT-LLM runs with the same override for the same reason.

framework_metadata.notes: Replaces blackwell-tp2-fa2: FlashAttention 2 on Blackwell is the slow exact kernel, and that profile was never validated (its notes said so); it published 141.04 s on minimax_h3_t2va_5s (4xGB300, 2026-10-10) against sglang's 57.46 s. LightX2V's MiniMax-H3 attention is single-segment (transformer_infer.py builds cu_seqlens = (0, seq_len)), so torch_sdpa -- cuDNN SDPA on sm_100/sm_103 -- computes the same attention. flash_attn4 also takes single-segment input, but the installer removes flash_attn.cute (no cutlass-dsl satisfies it). Probed 2026-10-12 on a 2xGB300 gb300-tml pod (LightX2V b6d38283, torch 2.14.1), minimax_h3_t2va_5s: torch_sdpa TP2 68.90 s, torch_sdpa Ulysses2 67.32 s, sglang main on the same pod 62.52 s. VALIDATION on a whole-node 4xGB300 pending.

framework_metadata.description: OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 per worker (VANILLA kept: 37742 rows split evenly).
framework_metadata.notes: Derived from `default` (the profile B300 selects). Audit 2026-10-23 (H3 finding 1): TRT-LLM spends 5 s (2 GPU), 8 s (Ref2VA) and 11 s (4 GPU) on the CPU before its denoise loop (row_timestep_plan: torch.full, scatters and torch.unique over the whole sequence per step, on every rank) while its workers share the host's cores with OMP_NUM_THREADS unset. The harness sets OMP_NUM_THREADS for no framework; sglang caps its workers itself (min(16, cores / GPUs), gpu_worker._worker_cpu_intra_op_threads), vLLM-Omni's workers take 1 (set_multiprocessing_worker_envs) and LightX2V's torchrun sets 1, while TRT-LLM and FastVideo keep one thread per core in every worker. Promoted from cand-omp8 by the 2026-10-22 4xB300 fourth-wave A/B: 69.63 s against 74.39 s: with OMP unset its 4 workers each keep one thread per core and lose 5-11 s per request to a CPU timestep plan before denoising.

framework_metadata.description: Blackwell: the default graph with every model resident on the GPU (--gpu-only).
framework_metadata.notes: B200: --gpu-only keeps every model, text encoders included, stored and run on the card; a 183 GB B200 holds the largest graph here (MiniMax-H3: 62 GB DiT + 48 GB Qwen3-VL-32B + VAEs). Placement only, numerics unchanged. Measured 2026-09-25 on 1xB200, FLUX.1 eager, interleaved arms: default 5.94 / 5.77 / 5.79s against --gpu-only 5.56s and --gpu-only --disable-dynamic-vram 5.57s (Qwen-Image-2.1: 3.75 / 3.91 against 3.47 / 3.48) -- every --gpu-only arm below every default arm; disabling dynamic VRAM on top adds nothing, so the simpler flag is kept.
